batch_notes: (1) Three targets (go-shellwords, go-toml, go-units) carry 'pin' properties written in property form (a property that picks one of a handful of fixed cases); tagged pin and categorised by what they assert, mostly spec-postcondition/rejection. go-yaml's 30 pins are plain example loops named without a Pin prefix. (2) Recurring shape the rubric does not name crisply: 'generated documents decode to the tree they were written from' (go-toml, go-yaml) -- a test-side writer produces text from a known tree and an external reader only arbitrates the generator; classified spec-postcondition (expected by construction) with oracle:external, but it sits between model-oracle and external-oracle. (3) go-json: 25 bugs, all pinned, no mentioned_by anywhere; only four are attributable via gating comments in property bodies, and most of the rest (NUL bytes, escape validation, HTMLEscape, 17-field structs, type-error continuation) look found by targeted probing rather than by the five oracle properties, hence many 'none'. The go-json README also records an oracle defect (Go 1.27.1 encoding/json.Indent hangs on an invalid input) that the property works around. (4) go-toml and go-yaml READMEs give one shared sentence for all nine general properties and no per-property doc comments; classifications there rest on bodies. go-shellquote's properties have empty doc comments. (5) go-version's precedence property gates around pinned pairs via a pinnedPair helper without citing bug ids, so bugs 1 and 2 are only 'inferred'. (6) Most attributable pins in this batch are gated by name rather than by bug id in property bodies (TestHegelPin... names), which the rubric's 'cites the bug id' wording does not literally cover; treated as explicit.
